title: fix(service-automation): a trigger binding does not dispatch a slot whose package is disabled (ADR-0150 D3)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zhuangjianguo"} -->
_Requested by **Steedos** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9Ubb?thread=cmsg_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9UbbCpddLFmKzR39wJWZpkRMCi)_
Fixes #33748

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no published skill teaches how a trigger binding behaves while a package is disabled (`skills/objectstack-automation` names a disabled package only for a packaged flow's queue approver)

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:两个包各带一个同名流程时,引擎按包各持一个槽位并各自挂触发器。现在触发器触发时引擎先问该槽位的包是否仍在服务:包被停用就不运行(不写运行记录、绝不换成另一个包的同名流程),每个槽位在停用期间只记一行 info;包重新启用后,同一个触发器直接恢复运行,无需重新挂载。
- 为什么改:座席裁决 6884403301 修正 3 写明「trigger binding: no dispatch」;PR #33646 落地了其余各门,唯独触发器这一路被推迟到本卡。
- 风险与回滚:只收窄一侧:停用包的槽位不再被触发器运行。槽位键、运行键、触发器绑定、`flowDispatchHolder` 都不动(修正 7),无需迁移。只有一个包持有的流程名不受影响(与 main 相同,另列为待决问题)。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts` 的 `triggerRun`(新增的停用判断与一次性日志)和 `isDisabledHolderSlot`(复用 `flowNameResolver` 的 `servedCaller` 读法)。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/flow-slots-per-package.test.ts`,预期 64 个全部通过,其中 `[#33748]` describe 共 13 个。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

A flow name two packages hold has one engine slot per holder (ADR-0150 D4), and each slot's trigger binding is armed under its own key. Every trigger family hands the engine one callback per binding, and that callback is the run `triggerRun` builds; `activateFlowTrigger` is the only `trigger.start` call site, so record-change, schedule, time-relative and the api inbound hook (whose queue consumer calls the armed callback) all reach it. Until now that run executed the armed slot with no served check (the deferred note of PR #33646).

- `packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts`, `triggerRun`: for a slot of a shared name with a package, the engine asks at fire time whether that package is disabled (`isDisabledHolderSlot`). If it is, nothing runs, no other slot is substituted, and the trigger's callback resolves with no result, so the caller logs no failure. The skip is said once per slot at `info` while its package stays disabled (the package switch working, nothing persisted is lost), and said again after the slot has dispatched once more. Asked at fire time, not at arming time: a runtime disable leaves the slot armed, so a re-enable dispatches it again with no re-arm.
- `isDisabledHolderSlot` (new, private): asks the one resolver (`flowNameResolver`) with the slot's package as the caller. Its own holding answers on the served read, and the run's read (`servedCaller`, amendment 4) answers `not-found` for it only while the package is disabled. Both readings are needed: `not-found` alone also covers a slot whose package the registry no longer holds the name for, which this rule does not judge (pinned as a CONTROL). No resolver attached: nothing is disabled, as before.
- Not touched: slot keys, run keys, the trigger bindings and `flowDispatchHolder` (amendment 7), and a slot of a name one package holds (it still runs through `execute`, as on `main`). No trigger plugin changes.

## Tests

`packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-slots-per-package.test.ts`, new top-level describe `[#33748] a trigger binding does not dispatch a slot whose package is disabled`, on the file's real `SchemaRegistry`, the real `flowNameResolver` and a recording trigger that fires each armed binding as a matching write would:

- In both registration orders, for each holder disabled: a runtime disable (both slots armed) dispatches only the served slot, the skip is said once over two fires with `{ flow, package, slot }` meta and no `error`; the slot keys, the dispatch holder and the bindings are unchanged; a re-enable dispatches both again with no new `start()`; a second disable is said again.
- In both orders, both disabled: nothing dispatches, each slot said once, keys unchanged.
- In both orders, for each holder: a boot disable (the disabled holder's flows not armed) never dispatches it; enabled and re-armed (the re-sync's `registerFlow`), both slots are armed under their qualified keys and both dispatch.
- CONTROLs: a shared name with nothing disabled (both dispatch, nothing said); two slots whose name the registry no longer holds (the resolver answers `not-found` for both packages, nothing is disabled: both dispatch, as on `main`); a name one package holds, enabled and disabled at runtime (it dispatches either way, as on `main`; see the open question below).

## Acceptance notes

- **A name one package holds, disabled at runtime (open question, not changed).** Its slot runs through `execute`, which serves it as on `main`; PR #33646 left the bare doors serving it too. Gating it here would move that answer for every single-holder package, which the ruling does not name; it is raised in the report with the four axes. In a composition whose disable door re-syncs the engine (the `metadata:reloaded` announce), the re-sync withdraws such a flow anyway.
- **The served holder of a shared name stays unarmed after a boot disable or a re-sync withdraw (finding, not changed).** Measured on this engine at `1e65a389`: with one holder disabled at boot (only the served holder shipped to the engine), the served holder's lone slot is filed under the bare key and declined by the M1 guard ("another package holds a flow named 't' whose body was refused"), so its trigger never dispatches. When a runtime disable is followed by the re-sync's `withdrawFlowSlot` of the disabled holder, the served slot's key moves from `PACKAGE/NAME` to the bare name and its binding is stopped and not re-armed. Both predate this PR; the boot-disable pins here assert only the disabled holder's half. Raised in the report for a separate card.
- **The inbound hook of a disabled holder's slot.** The trigger-api member's queue consumer calls the armed callback, so a queued post for that slot is skipped by the same check. What the hook door answers the sender for such a slot (`inboundHookSlot`, admission) is not moved here and was not measured.

The boot-disable pins stay green under A1, as expected: they pin that the disabled holder is not armed, which this PR does not change.
